name: PhotoCraft
tagline: A free, open-source photo editor that works like Photoshop - runs on your computer, no subscription, no account.
sentence: Open a photo, add layers, masks and adjustment layers the same way you would in Photoshop, but without paying Adobe $23 a month.

visual.alt: PhotoCraft editing Hokusai's Great Wave: 6 layers in the layers panel, a Curves adjustment layer open, and a full toolbar with selection, brush and shape tools on the left.
visual.caption: The editor with a classic woodcut, showing layers, a curves adjustment and the full Photoshop-style toolbar.

board.say: You need to edit photos - crop, adjust colors, combine layers, remove backgrounds - but Photoshop costs $23 a month and the free alternatives feel different.
board.eg: You want to composite two images: cut out a subject, drop it onto a new background, and adjust the colors so they match.

board.say: You open PhotoCraft on your computer, or an AI agent opens it through its built-in command interface.
board.eg: Double-click the app, or type a command in Claude Code - PhotoCraft has over 500 commands an agent can call.

board.say: Your photo files: JPEG, PNG, PSD, TIFF, WebP, RAW and more - including Photoshop's own layered files.
board.eg: Open a PSD file from a designer and keep all the layers, masks and adjustment layers intact.

board.say: It gives you a full editing workspace with layers, masks, brushes and adjustments, all running locally.
steps: Pick from 52 tools: selection, brush, pen, shape, text, gradient, eyedropper and more
Stack layers, masks and 16 adjustment layers (Curves, Levels, Hue/Saturation) with 27 blend modes
Apply filters with live previews, or transform and warp with full undo history
Save as PSD, TIFF, PNG, JPEG or WebP - with PSD files round-tripping cleanly (134 of 135 test files preserved)
board.eg: The README demo: open a multi-layer PSD, adjust the curves, paint on a mask, and save - the file comes back usable in Photoshop.

board.say: An edited photo or layered project file, saved on your own computer.

outputs.eg: A JPEG or PNG ready to post, or a layered PSD you can hand off to a designer
Every adjustment layer and mask is preserved - come back tomorrow and change anything
The same workflow Photoshop charges $23/month for, running on your machine for free

before: Editing photos with layers, masks and color adjustments means paying Adobe $23 a month - or learning a free tool that works differently.
Opening a designer's PSD file means owning Photoshop, or losing layers and adjustments in a converter.
after: The same layers-and-masks workflow, on your own computer, for free - with keyboard shortcuts Photoshop users already know.
Open PSD files with layers intact, edit them, and save back without losing anything.
uses_note: PhotoCraft is 9 days old and in early alpha. Named real-world use is still very early.

coverage.title: ArtCraft Apps - open-source Rust alternatives to Adobe's creative suite

steps: [Download PhotoCraft](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/releases) for your computer (Mac, Windows or Linux) and install it.

Open a photo and try the basics: crop it, open a [Curves adjustment layer](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft#non-destructive-adjustments) (Image > Adjustments > Curves), and paint on a mask to apply the adjustment to only part of the image.
Try opening a Photoshop PSD file if you have one - check that the layers, masks and adjustments come through.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/storytold/photocraft

If that scan passes: download and install PhotoCraft, open a sample image, add a Curves adjustment layer, and try the brush tool on a layer mask. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No data found for installer size. The source code builds with `cargo run --release -p photocraft` (requires Rust 1.90+).
footprint.memory: No data found. Uses a GPU compositor (Metal, Vulkan or DirectX 12) and falls back to all CPU cores without a GPU.
footprint.runs_on: Mac (universal), Windows (x64, arm64, x86), Linux (x86_64, aarch64), FreeBSD and the web (via WebAssembly). Installers: DMG, MSI, AppImage, Flatpak, DEB, RPM.

best_for: You know Photoshop's workflow and want a free alternative that works the same way - layers, masks, adjustment layers, the same shortcuts
You want to edit photos on your own machine without an account, a subscription or an internet connection
skip_if: You need a battle-tested editor for paid client work today - this is in early alpha and its creator says it is 'not anywhere close to ready'
You rely on Photoshop plugins or advanced features like generative AI fill - those are not built yet

alternatives.name: GIMP
alternatives.line: The established free photo editor. More stable and complete, but a different interface - not a Photoshop look-alike.

alternatives.name: Photopea
alternatives.line: A free browser-based editor that opens PSD files. No install needed, but it runs in the cloud, not on your machine.

alternatives.name: Krita
alternatives.line: A free painting and illustration app. Stronger for digital art and drawing, lighter on photo-editing features.

watch: **Early alpha - not ready for professional work.** The creator says it is 'not anywhere close to ready.' Users report lag, frozen tools and broken keyboard shortcuts. Expect bugs.

**Built almost entirely by one person using AI.** Brandon Thomas, a developer from Atlanta, built these apps using Claude Opus 5.5 as his AI coding assistant. The repo shows two committers, one with over 550K lines. Long-term maintenance is an open question.

**5 of this week's 10 picks are from the same maker.** PhotoCraft is part of the ArtCraft suite by storytold. That concentration reflects a real moment - four Adobe replacements launched at once - but it means one org's fate affects half this edition.
**Well under 50% of Photoshop's depth.** All 625 menu items are wired, but many are stubs. Missing: generative AI features, deep typography, about 20 tools, and plug-in compatibility.
